summary: Bend proofs are plain dependently-typed defs: no tactics, one rewrite form (%e : goal-with-_), {==} for conversion, recursion as IH. Shipped evidence at 565d7fd: 15 demos / 43 laws / 1839 lines (LAWS 399, PROOF 1440); 12 of 43 laws close by {==} alone, the rest need 1-6 helper lemmas each, every rewrite spelling its whole motive. Recurring costs: computed verdicts cannot be matched in place so each case split becomes a ".fin" helper def; Base ships no Nat.add lemmas so add_zero/add_succ/add_comm are re-proven in 4 demos and 2 evals; programs are restructured for provability (evidence-returning comparisons, verdict parameters); law parameters carry +/- quantity marks the human must choose from how the proof will spend them. Checking is cheap (0.10-0.20 s; 3.8 s for a 2800-line game). 4 of 15 demo PROOF.bend files print SOME PROOFS FAIL at this commit because an @unsafe def exists in the imported program, contradicting the GUIDE's "ALL PROOFS CHECK once every law holds"; a 13-line test confirms one unrelated @unsafe def alone flips the gate. CHANGELOG: 36 releases in 17 days, 4 closed-Empty soundness holes fixed, verdict text changed twice, --safe renamed --verdict. My own proofs: wrong one yields "expected : 1n / observed : 0n"; correct length_append took 1 attempt (idiom copied from two shipped proofs), 16 lines, 0.127 s check, 0.132 s --verdict.

facts.claim: Bend has no tactics; a proof is a def whose type is the claim; the only proof forms are {==}, %e : P rewrite with _ marking the rewritten term, match, recursive call as IH, exs witness as a pair, ?TODO hole.
facts.quote: Bend has no tactics: a proposition is a type, and a proof is a def of that type.

facts.claim: GUIDE CLAIMS the gate prints ALL PROOFS CHECK once every law holds.
facts.quote: it prints SOME PROOFS FAIL while any law is open or false, and ALL PROOFS CHECK once every law holds

facts.claim: CODE DOES: 4 of 15 shipped demo PROOF.bend files print SOME PROOFS FAIL with every law filled, because defs in the imported program rely on @unsafe: pure_hvm5_mini (35 defs), app_slash_boss_3d (4), io_http_server (2), io_tcp_echos (4). Listed defs are all main.* program defs, none a Laws.* fill. Other 11 demos print ALL PROOFS CHECK.
facts.quote: the accept loop is @unsafe: it runs until killed

facts.claim: Confirmed in isolation: a law closed by {==} beside one unrelated @unsafe def the law never mentions prints SOME PROOFS FAIL / Error: 1 def relies on unsafe or foreign code: / - spin (exit 1). Scratch file unsafe_beside_law.bend, 13 lines.
CHANGELOG 2.0.32 states the rule the code follows (narrower than the GUIDE sentence): a proof holds only with no @unsafe and no user foreign code, imports included.
facts.quote: A proof holds when bend checks it and it uses no `@unsafe` def and no user foreign code, imports included. `--verdict` (was `--safe`)

facts.claim: Tier = solution length (lines after '# solution'): cake 8/16/25/13; easy 56/47/56/56; firm 74/105/64/80; hard 178/230/287/159; hell 386/270/540/747. Check times 0.11-0.20 s at every tier.

facts.claim: Test runner compares exactly the '#|' lines; failure is detected by the regex /^(SOME PROOFS FAIL|Error:)/, so tests pin error text verbatim and any change to checker wording or goal rendering breaks pinned tests.

Correct proof: length of append over Base List<&2, Nat>, 16 lines total, def 7 lines, 1 attempt, --check-only ALL PROOFS CHECK in 0.127 s, --verdict ALL PROOFS CHECK in 0.132 s. Theory has one universe and no positivity check; consistency rests on a live/dead wall; dead code may inhabit Empty.
facts.quote: Dead code may loop forever or inhabit `Empty`, but nothing dead ever counts as live evidence

Whether a PROOF.bend for any program with a server loop can ever print ALL PROOFS CHECK without splitting the pure part into a separate file the proofs import (the demos did not do this; 4/15 ship failing).

Scaling of rewrite motives: the longest shipped motive lines (~200 chars) occur at 2-3 IH rewrites; no shipped evidence shows a proof past hell-tier 747 lines or a law over a state record wider than Slash.Game's 11 fields.

Which of the 33 pinned-failure tests pin error wording that a fidelity gate would need to parse; the goal-ladder pages suggest the rendered goal text is treated as a stable interface but the CHANGELOG shows it changed in 2.0.29 ('Errors underline their span').
